title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
abstract: arXiv:2610.35193v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. translated_title: 大模型时代可信赖的递归自我改进：基础、风险、评估与开放挑战
translated_abstract: 以大模型为核心的AI系统越来越多地利用经验和反馈对模型、提示词、记忆、工具和工作流程进行持久性修改。递归自我改进（RSI）将这一过程进一步扩展到归纳偏置以及支配未来更新的机制，而这些机制本身也可以在改进循环中被修订和复用。然而，仅靠自我修改并不能保证可信赖的改进：所报告的性能提升可能源于有缺陷的评估；先前获得的能力可能出现退化；对行为约束的遵从可能减弱；受损的组件或敏感信息也可能在后续系统中持续存在；对改进机制的更改可能使早期的验证结果失效，并削弱人类监督的有效性。本综述给出了RSI的操作性定义与过程框架，并将可信赖RSI的需求归纳为四个相互关联的主题：真正的……（原文摘要到此截断）
tldr: 本文提出了递归自我改进（RSI）的操作性定义与过程框架，系统梳理了大模型时代实现可信赖自我改进所涉及的基础、风险、评估需求与开放挑战。
en_tdlr: This survey provides an operational definition and process framework for recursive self-improvement (RSI), systematically organizing the foundations, risks, evaluation requirements, and open challenges for achieving trustworthy self-improvement in the era of large models.
